Why are plane windows round? Because the square ones tore three jets apart.
Nineteen fifty-two. The de Havilland Comet. The first jet airliner in the world, and it had big, square windows.
Within two years, three of them came apart in mid air.
Here is what was happening. Up high, the cabin is pumped up like a balloon, and every flight stretches the metal a little.
In a curve, that stress flows around the bend. In a corner, it piles up in one spot.
At the corner of a square window it was roughly three times higher. A crack started there, and one day it ran.
So they put a whole fuselage in a water tank, pumped it until it burst, and found it.
Every airliner window since has had rounded corners. No window has done it again.
So that little oval next to you is not a style choice. It is the most redesigned piece of glass in history.
And it is still the best seat. Send this to whoever always takes it.
